title: read past the end of the allocator's own backing block
object: a, 24 bytes; the access is at a + st_alloc_pool_bytes() + 8192
offset_bytes: st_alloc_pool_bytes() + 8192, or 24 when the allocator has no pool
note: The Tier-1 analogue of corpus/real cases 29 and 31, whose fuzz images over-read about 2 KB and leave the 256 KiB memsys5 arena entirely. Detection here says the access escaped the container, not that the tool understands the container.

asan.why: The pool is one malloc block, so an access past its end is an ordinary heap-buffer-overflow of that block. Every malloc-granular tool recovers its sight; the annotation columns add nothing.

valgrind.why: Same: the byte is outside the block Memcheck tracks.

hwasan.why: The access lands 8192 bytes past the backing block (past a itself on malloc), in memory with another tag, so every column is DETECTED whatever the allocator tags inside its pool.

ubsan.why: -fsanitize=bounds needs a statically known array bound; a pointer out of an allocator has none. The row is kept so the report can say UBSan is not a heap tool rather than leaving it out.

lowfat.why: On malloc the offset degenerates to 24, inside the size class, so LowFat misses its own baseline (see case 1). Past the pool it is far outside the pool's class and LowFat reports.

status: written, smoke-run on malloc, arena and freelist; server run pending (A5)
